stops.note: 'day of Saturn', god of sowing, whose December festival was the Saturnalia
the one English day that kept the Roman god's name instead of a Germanic substitute; Dutch zaterdag did the same, while German Samstag comes from 'Sabbath'
Britain's Factory Act of 1850 ended textile mill work at 2 pm on Saturdays, the start of the Saturday half-holiday

current_meaning: the day of the week before Sunday
